answer: Rate-limited reward vesting forces new agents to wait before cashing out. Each identity must complete tasks over weeks to unlock tokens—a falcon-speed attacker spawning thousands hits immediate compute and registration costs while rewards drip slowly. The system treats reputation like an onyx stone: dense, earned grain by grain. A sybil farm bleeding operational expenses for thirty days before first payout makes mass identity creation a relic strategy—break-even arrives only after sustained work per agent.
